title: PB06425-001 MM Post Transplant 1 year
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.
description: Library name: PB06425-001
H5 file contains RNA expression matrix
data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB05006-002 MM Post Transplant 1 year
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB06427-003 Flu Year 1 Day 90
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB00240-01 MM Post Transplant 60 Days
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB01323-01 Flu Year 1 Day 0
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB01348-01 MM Pre-Treatment
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02053-01 Flu Year 2 Stand-Alone
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02064-01 Flu Year 2 Day 7
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02084-01 Flu Year 2 Day 90
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02733-001 Flu Year 1 Day 0
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02767-001 Flu Year 1 Stand-Alone
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB04689-002 MM Pre-Treatment
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB04828-001 MM Post Transplant 60 Days
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB05124-001 MM Post Transplant 60 Days
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB06438-001 MM End Induction 1st Draw
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02089-04 MM CD38 Pre-treatment
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02722-002 MM CD38 4 weeks
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02749-002 MM CD38 4 weeks
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB02774-002 MM CD38 4 weeks
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB04841-002 MM CD38 Pre-treatment
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.

data_processing: Multiplexed sequencing data were prepared using a preprocessing pipeline based on 10x Genomics CellRanger software (version 3.1.0; Released July 24, 2019), with the 10x Genomics GRCh38/hg38 Human Transcriptome Reference (refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-3.0.0; based on the GRCh38 genome reference and Ensembl v93 transcriptome annotations; Released Nov. 19, 2018) to generate cell x UMI count matrices for each Well.

To identify cells originating from each sample, we utilized software tools for HTO quantification and sample demultiplexing to generate separate HDF5-formatted files for each originating sample (as described in Swanson, et al. (2021); DOI: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2). This process also removes Cell Barcodes that contain HTOs from multiple samples (doublets or multiplets) or with no detectable sample label (no hash).

After demultiplexing, data from individual samples assembled across all hashed wells were given a first pass of cell type labels using Seurat label transfer with reference to the PBMC dataset provided by the Satija Lab (Stuart and Butler, et al. (2019); DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.031) and provided online with the Seurat PBMC scATAC-seq vignette (v 3.0; Compiled June 6, 2019).

For analysis, high quality cells were selected based on the following cutoffs: <10% mitochondria reads, number of genes detected between 200 and 5000, RNA UMIs/cells between 1500 and 750000. After QC filtering, all remaining cells were clustered using a Scanpy (v1.9.6) workflow that consisted of normalization using scanpy.pp.normalize_total with the parameter target_sum = 1e4; log transformation using scanpy.pp.log1p; highly variable gene detection using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes; scaling of highly variable gene data using sc.pp.scale; Dimensionality reduction using scanpy.tl.pca with the parameter svd_solver = 'arpack'.
Supplementary files format and content: Ensembl GRCh38-3.0.0
Supplementary files format and content: h5 files, gene expression matrix

title: PB05134-001 MM CD38 9 months
extract_protocol_ch1: PBMCs were removed from liquid nitrogen and rapidly thawed in a 37°C water bath. Cells were diluted dropwise into 40 mL AIM V media (Thermo Fisher Scientific) pre-warmed to 37°C. Cells were pelleted at 400 x g for 5–10 min at 4–10°C, resuspended in 5 mL cold AIM V media, and counted using a Cellometer Spectrum or Cellaca. After adding 30 mL cold AIM V media, cells were re-pelleted and resuspended to the appropriate concentrations for scRNAseq.

scRNAseq libraries were generated using a modified 10x genomics chromium 3′ single cell gene expression assay with Cell Hashing. Sample libraries were constructed across different batches, with the addition of a common healthy donor leukopak sample in each library as batch control. Libraries were sequenced on the Illumina Novaseq platform. Hashed 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data processing was carried out using BarWare (BMC Bioinformatics 2022, doi: 10.1186/s12859-022-04620-2) to generate sample-specific output files.
